next_steps: Redwood to share incident timeline doc and raw logs (Riya) by 2026-07-02
Aurora to run benchmark with patch on staging and share perf numbers by 2026-07-07
Schedule on-site/zoom deep-dive for network config with Aurora infra team (Alex) week of 2026-07-06
Redwood security pack (SOC2 + KMS config) link shared (Marcus) by 2026-07-01
action_items: Riya Patel: collect server-level gpu traces and KV cache metrics; due 2026-07-02

summary: Follow-up postmortem after 2026-06-28 production latency spike. Root cause appears to be a combination of a model rollout to a larger sequence length and a degraded network path causing rejections and cache churn. Agreed mitigations: rollback model variant in prod, tighten rollout windows, add KV-cache telemetry, and run network path tests. Redwood to provide logs and a staging benchmark; Aurora to test patch and validate SLA impacts.
topics: Long-term reliability improvements (rollout policy, automated fallback)
transcript:
Head: Date: 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Riya Patel, Marcus Li (Redwood); Sofia Martinez, Daniel Ortiz, Priya Rao, Tom Bennett (Aurora)

00:00 - Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to do a quick postmortem follow up from the 6/28 spike, go over timeline and next steps.
00:15 - Sofia Martinez: yeah thanks alex. we had a pretty bad customer impact friday morning, about 30-45s extra latency on a bunch of routes and some rps drops. we opened a ticket with your support and saw a bunch of 5xxs.
00:28 - Riya Patel: sorry can you say the duration again, 30 to 45 seconds extra latency?
00:31 - Sofia Martinez: right, per request, but it spiked across many calls leading to backpressure.
00:45 - Daniel Ortiz: to add, the batch sizes also ballooned because some inference requests had much longer sequence lengths due to a new prompt template we rolled out.
01:02 - Riya Patel: ok that's useful. we saw a model variant rollout at 02:13 UTC that increased predicted token counts; combined with a transient network flapping between their region and us, it caused increased KV-cache miss rates. there might be some transcription error in our logs that calls it 'KK cache' in the exporter - we'll annotate.
01:28 - Priya Rao: one concern from security is if any data replays or duplication happened during retries. we did a cursory check and didn't find obvious replays but need deeper audit.
01:45 - Marcus Li: we will provide the complete request/response logs (redacted) and timeline; Riya will own the GPU traces.
02:00 - Tom Bennett: did you see any correlation with autoscaling events? our metrics show some pods were restarted around the same time.
02:12 - Riya Patel: yes there were a couple of infra restarts in the Dedicated pool - looks like a flapping network route caused failed healthchecks and a few pods restarted; that in turn caused more load on remaining pods which exacerbated latency.
02:35 - Alex Chen: so prelim root cause: model rollout to a higher sequence expectation + network path degradation leading to cache churn and pod restarts -> overload.
03:01 - Sofia Martinez: is there any sign this is related to our VPC peering? we changed a routing rule last week.
03:18 - Daniel Ortiz: we did tweak SNAT settings last Wednesday; could be related, maybe the egress path changed.
03:32 - Riya Patel: we'll correlate with the network team but from our side two mitigations helped in prod: 1) rollback model variant to previous quantized version, 2) temporarily increase concurrency limit per pod to smooth the backlog. after rollback errors dropped from 12% to 1.8% and p95 latency returned close to baseline.
03:58 - Sofia Martinez: thanks, that rollback stabilized. our ask is a clear prevention plan and better visibility — specifically KV cache misses, per-model seq-length distribution, and network path health.
04:20 - Marcus Li: agreed. we can add KV cache metrics to the route dashboard and add a seq-length histogram to model telemetry. we'll also provide A/B rollout safeguards.
04:45 - Tom Bennett: can we have a canary window that only lets 1% traffic to new variants for 24hrs?
05:00 - Riya Patel: yes; we have a rollout policy that supports percent-based canaries and automatic rollback on error thresholds, but it wasn't enabled for that variant. we'll make percent-canaries default for production-moving variants.
05:28 - Daniel Ortiz: what about automated fallback to quantized model if latency degrades?
05:40 - Riya Patel: we can set up a fallback policy to a compatible model family; that will add a small routing cost but will preserve availability.
06:03 - Priya Rao: on security checks, thanks for the redaction plan. also want to confirm KMS usage — we expect logs and payloads encrypted at rest and in transit; can you send the KMS proof?
06:20 - Marcus Li: yes will share the SOC2 + KMS configuration doc. linking that as an action.
06:33 - Alex Chen: quick note on telemetry gaps: we didn't have high-resolution KV-cache miss rates around the incident; our exporter sampling might have been too coarse - we'll bump to 1s for a short window in prod when we run bench tests.
06:55 - Sofia Martinez: that would be great. also, some of our alerting thresholds didn't trigger because the metrics were averaged across pods; we need per-pod alerting on queue depth and p99 latency.
07:10 - Riya Patel: good call; we'll push per-pod metrics and create runbook playbooks for these alerts so your on-call knows remediation steps.
07:28 - Tom Bennett: how about the cost tradeoffs — increasing telemetry and percent-canaries will add some cost. we'll need to justify that.
07:45 - Alex Chen: understood. Redwood can provide an estimate of additional token/infra cost for running higher-resolution telemetry and a fallback pool. we'll include that in the follow-up.
08:02 - Daniel Ortiz: a more structural ask: can Redwood provide a 'guardrail' that prevents large sequence-length bursts from being sent to production? maybe limit max tokens or auto-split requests?
08:25 - Riya Patel: we can implement a pre-filter on the API gateway to either truncate or split oversized prompts and optionally return a warning. that would be configurable.
08:42 - Priya Rao: does that change any data residency or compliance constraints? truncation is fine but we want to ensure no PII is accidentally modified.
08:55 - Marcus Li: truncation would be policy-based and would not persist before passing through encryption; we'll document the behavior.
09:12 - Sofia Martinez: timeline review: could you walk through the exact minute-by-minute? we need that for our audit.
09:25 - Riya Patel: yes — 02:05 UTC initial batch of long-seq requests, 02:13 model variant rollout, 02:17 first pod healthcheck failures, 02:22 retries started piling, 02:30 elevated 5xx and queue growth, 02:43 rollback initiated by Redwood support, 02:50 error rates back down. we'll publish the full timeline with raw logs.
10:00 - Tom Bennett: any indication of data loss?
10:10 - Riya Patel: no persistent loss observed; some client retries resulted in duplicate downstream calls but nothing persisted to durable stores. we'll verify with audit logs.
10:28 - Daniel Ortiz: ok good. longer-term, we want automated regression detection in your model catalog — if a variant causes a >10% p95 regression vs baseline in staging, block rollout.
10:50 - Alex Chen: that's reasonable; we'll extend our rollout policy to include regression gating and make staging promotion require a health check pass.
11:05 - Priya Rao: on the legal/compliance side, procurement asked for a note that fallback behavior and logs will be retained for 90 days and available for audits. is that acceptable?
11:18 - Marcus Li: yes we'll confirm retention windows; default is 30 days but we can offer 90 day on enterprise plan with audit exports.
11:30 - Sofia Martinez: thanks. any other technical mitigations we should track?
11:36 - Riya Patel: add KV cache telemetry, per-pod metrics, percent-canaries default, automatic fallback to quantized model, API pre-filter for oversized prompts, and network path monitoring.
12:02 - Alex Chen: great. let's assign action items — Riya will push telemetry changes and provide GPU traces; Marcus will share security docs; Alex will coordinate the benchmark schedule.
12:25 - Sofia Martinez: we'll run the staging benchmark after you share the test harness. expected to take 48-72hrs to validate.
12:40 - Tom Bennett: one last question - is there anything we should change in our client retries? we have exponential backoff but tight retry counts.
12:55 - Riya Patel: recommend smaller retry counts on 5xx (2 attempts) plus jitter, and prefer idempotency keys when possible. we'll share recommended client config.
13:12 - Daniel Ortiz: thanks. also please include the code snippet for the pre-filter so our infra can review.
13:25 - Riya Patel: will do.
13:35 - Alex Chen: recap of next steps and owners — we'll put all docs in a shared confluence and send invite for the deep-dive.
13:48 - Sofia Martinez: good, thanks everyone.
14:00 - (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KK cache) and shorthand; timestamps are approximate. Links referenced during call: /redwood/logs/incident-90872 (redacted), /redwood/bench/harness.zip (attachment), Redwood SOC2 summary (shared PDF).
